name: Apache Fory (Swift)
baseline: Codable with Foundation JSONEncoder / JSONDecoder (macOS 15.7.2); SwiftProtobuf also compared
verdict_reason: Its reproducible benchmark shows 11x-59x the throughput of JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder and 1.65x-5.57x that of SwiftProtobuf on six data shapes. The numbers are first-party, but the harness and run script are public.
tier_reason: Benchmark source and run script (swift build -c release) are in the repo and the page states OS build, cores and memory; first-party.
claimed_speedup: vs JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder: NumericStruct serialize 14,759,606 vs 481,278 ops/s (30.7x), deserialize 18,155,795 vs 377,802 (48.1x); MediaContent serialize 2,987,821 vs 111,200 (26.9x), deserialize 1,072,345 vs 97,799 (11.0x) (JSON ratios derived from page data). vs SwiftProtobuf: from fory (1.65x) on Sample deserialize to fory (5.57x) on MediaContentList serialize.
workload: Serialize and deserialize six model shapes (struct of 12 int32 fields, mixed struct with arrays, nested media object graph, and lists of each) for 3 s per case
metric: throughput (operations per second) and payload size
hardware: MacBook Pro, 12 logical cores, 48 GB (chip not named)
toolchain: swift build -c release (run.sh); Swift version not stated
one_liner: Macro-generated cross-language binary serializer; 11-59x the throughput of Codable JSON and up to 5.6x SwiftProtobuf in its own benchmark.
how_it_is_fast: Swift macros (@ForyStruct, @ForyEnum, @ForyUnion) generate a serializer per type at compile time that writes fields in a fixed order into a compact binary format with variable-length integers. At runtime there are no key strings and no Codable container existentials. The same xlang format is readable from Java, Python, Rust, Go and other Fory runtimes.
use_it_when: Object serialization where you control both ends, in-process or across languages
Object graphs with shared or circular references (trackRef)
skip_it_when: Builds that cannot take a swift-syntax macro dependency
caveats: First-party benchmark; Fory wins every row of its own table.
CPU model not named; one run of 3 s per case.
Repository star count covers the whole multi-language project, not the Swift package.
tradeoffs: Depends on swift-syntax for its macros, which adds build time
Fory-specific wire format; some payloads are larger than protobuf's (Sample: 445 vs 375 bytes)
